data.title: Applied Digital (APLD) Stock Trades Up, Here Is Why
data.description:
What Happened?

Shares of digital infrastructure provider Applied Digital jumped 4.6% in the afternoon session after the company announced their second phase of Building 2 at its Polaris Forge 1 campus in Ellendale, North Dakota, reached Ready for Service. According the company press release, the addition brings 75 MW of critical IT load across three 25 MW halls, completing Building 2’s 150 MW and lifting the campus’s fully operational critical IT load to 250 MW. The full 400 MW campus is fully leased.

After the initial pop, the shares cooled down to $25.13, up 4% from the previous close.

What Is The Market Telling Us

Applied Digital’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 98 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock dropped 5.2% on the news that Rothschild & Co Redburn initiated coverage of the company with a Neutral rating and a $22 price target, adding to caution ahead of earnings. According to TipRanks, Redburn analyst Alex Haissl started coverage with Neutral and a $22 target, flagging execution, power, and pipeline-conversion risks. TipRanks / The Fly reported that Jones Trading analyst Kevin Dede separately initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $70 price target, citing Applied Digital’s shift toward AI datacenters and investment-grade customers. The conflicting Street views weighed on the stock ahead of the company’s fiscal first-quarter 2027 results, scheduled for October 8, even as peers in digital infrastructure also faced broader rate and inflation pressure.

Applied Digital is down 10.6% since the beginning of the year, and at $25.13 per share, it is trading 49.4% below its 52-week high of $49.65 from May 2026. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Applied Digital’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,948.

data.title: The G-7 Oil Bailout Is Surprisingly Good News for Energy Stocks — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Avi Salzman

The latest stopgap solution to the global energy crisis is positive news for energy companies-even if it looks bad at first glance.

Energy stocks initially fell on Friday on news that the Group of Seven major economies plan to release up to 100 million barrels of diesel fuel and crude oil into the market. If the G-7's bailout eases the oil and fuel shortage, it will force prices lower and reduce profits.

But most of the stocks rebounded in less than an hour. The short-term negative looks like it could result in long-term gains.

ExxonMobil was up 0.2%, after initially falling more than 1%. Refiner Valero was off just 1% after dropping more than 4%.

On net, it's good news for energy companies.

They had been facing a much more severe threat, which now looks much less likely. President Donald Trump was pushing for a U.S. diesel export ban that could have forced American refineries to throttle back their operations. The energy industry came out strongly against the plan.

The G-7 statement said that "we reaffirm our commitment to refrain from export restrictions on energy and energy products between G7 countries." (The U.S. is in the G-7.)

By comparison, the G-7's stockpile release is a more mild and temporary solution to a broader problem that still hasn't been fixed, like taking a Tylenol for a fever that's likely to come back a few hours later.

The broader diesel market is still undersupplied, and should remain so-this week, Russia extended a diesel export ban until the end of October.

Until the wars in Iran and Russia are over, the diesel market is unlikely to return to normal.

What's more, the G-7 release sets up a situation where demand is likely to be even higher in the future. If European countries sell off their stockpiles of fuel now, they will have to buy even more in the future to refill the tanks.

Today's bailout could lead to more profits tomorrow.

data.title: Nymex Overview: Petroleum Futures Falling on News of Planned G7 Inventory Release — OPIS
data.description:
Crude oil and refined product futures contracts were seeing sharp declines Friday amid increased optimism over Middle East oil supply and news that the Group of Seven nations plan a substantial release from diesel and crude stockpiles to combat record-high prices.

U.S. oil prices were down about 2.4% at 11:45 a.m. ET, with the November West Texas Intermediate crude prices down $2.12 to $90.75/bbl and December prices trading $1.98 lower to $88.91/bbl.

Brent crude losses were lighter, with the December contract moving 96cts lower to $101.35/bbl and January prices sinking by 68cts to $97.75/bbl.

Diesel futures were falling by about 3.8%, with November prices off by 17.5cts to $4.467/gal and the December contract 16.45cts lower to $4.3261/gal.

RBOB futures were trading down 3.4%, with the November contract sinking by 11.54cts to $3.2872/gal and December prices moving 8.4cts lower to $3.0889/gal.

If the declines hold, they will snap a two-day streak of solid gains for both crude and ULSD.

Prices are weakening after the G7 nations said they planned to release 100 million barrels from their stored reserves of diesel and crude over the next four months.

A statement from the group encouraged countries with significant refining capacity to boost production. It said member countries will also "coordinate maintenance schedules across G7 refineries to prevent simultaneous capacity shutdowns and temporarily increase utilization rates where feasible."

The move comes as U.S. President Donald Trump has been criticizing European leaders, saying they have not significantly tapped into their reserves to help address rising fuel costs amid the Iran war.

Prices are also being pressured by recent news of larger-than-expected oil shipments from the Middle East, even as uncertainty remains about the future of the ongoing Iranian conflict.

Petroleum prices had moved higher earlier in the week following reports the U.S. was sending a third aircraft carrier to the region, raising the possibility of an impending increase in fighting.

data.title: Biogen's experimental lupus drug shows benefit against skin symptoms
data.description:
Biogen said on Friday its experimental drug showed durable improvement in skin symptoms among patients with a type of autoimmune disease in a mid-stage study.

Here are some details:

  • Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) can cause painful rashes, sensitivity to sunlight, hair loss, skin discoloration and permanent scarring. There are no approved targeted treatments for the condition.

  • The company said 27.2% of participants who received the drug, litifilimab, from the beginning of the trial had clear or almost clear skin after one year, compared with 19% after 24 weeks.

  • Litifilimab is also being tested for lupus and other forms of the autoimmune condition.

  • The trial results come as Biogen faces mounting pressure on its legacy multiple sclerosis portfolio from pricing challenges and competition, prompting it to rely on newer products, including Alzheimer's drug Leqembi, to revive growth.

  • Nearly 29% of patients achieved at least a 70% reduction in skin disease activity at week 52, up from 21.7% at week 24, Biogen said.

  • Litifilimab was generally well tolerated with no new safety concerns identified, it said.

  • The mid-stage trial enrolled 93 adults whose skin symptoms had not responded to, or who could not tolerate, standard antimalarial medicines.

  • The most common side effects included common cold-like infections, influenza and joint pain.

  • Biogen said litifilimab aims to suppress inflammation by targeting BDCA2 receptors found on plasmacytoid dendritic cells, which are immune cells that trigger and regulate the body's defense mechanisms.

  • Biogen expects results from the late-stage part of the study in the first half of 2027.

data.title: Tesla Stock Jumps After Surprise Q3 Delivery Beat
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) shares rose about 3% Friday morning trading after the electric-vehicle maker reported third-quarter deliveries that exceeded its latest company-compiled analyst estimate.

The company delivered 486,532 vehicles during the quarter, up from 480,126 in the second quarter but below the 497,099 vehicles delivered a year earlier. Tesla's Sept. 29 compilation had projected 461,974 deliveries, based on 24 analyst estimates.

Production totaled 464,391 vehicles, leaving deliveries above output for the quarter. Reuters reported that the delivery result benefited from improved European sales, while demand remained weaker in the United States and China.

The update arrives as Tesla focuses increasingly on businesses beyond conventional vehicle sales. The company has expanded its robotaxi operations and is developing the Cybercab and Optimus humanoid robot, while its Full Self-Driving system continues to expand geographically.

Tesla will report full third-quarter financial results after the market closes on Oct. 21. The company cautioned that vehicle deliveries are only one measure of quarterly performance and do not provide a complete view of earnings or cash flow.

data.title: Nvidia, Tesla, Rivian, On Semi, Seagate, HPE, Nike, and More Stocks That Explain Today's Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
By George Glover and Mariapaula Gonzalez

Stocks rose Friday and bond yields dropped as U.S. monthly jobs report for September was weaker than expected, easing expectations for a potential rate hike by the Federal Reserve.

Nvidia advanced 2.8%. Shares were on pace to close at a record high, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The company recently added a historic $150 billion to its share repurchase program.

Tesla rose 4.2% after the electric-vehicle maker delivered 486,532 cars in its fiscal third quarter. The figure, which is up 1% from the second quarter and down 2% year over year, smashed Wall Street's estimates of 450,000 to 460,000 deliveries.

Rivian Automotive fell 3.3%. The EV manufacturer delivered 19,248 vehicles in the fiscal third quarter, topping consensus estimates of 18,001.

ON Semiconductor rose 5.8% after the chip supplier agreed to buy Synaptics for $5.7 billion in cash, compared with $7 billion in stock previously. Synaptics shares rallied 15% ahead.

Nike slumped 6.1%. The retailer missed Wall Street's first-quarter revenue target and issued downbeat fiscal-year guidance as its turnaround flounders.

Cryptocurrency stocks got a boost as Bitcoin traded back above $86,000. Strategy rose 4.2%, Coinbase Global advanced 1.8%, and Robinhood Markets added 3.8%. The move came after Fed Vice Chairman Philip Jefferson said Thursday that the central bank needs more time to gauge economic health before making any further rate adjustments.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise advanced 5.9% and was the top gainer in the S&P 500. The company said Wednesday it projects solid revenue growth for its networking business segment because of AI demand.

Seagate Technology tumbled 13% and was the worst performer in the S&P 500. A recent report from Nikkei revealed that Toshiba will double its production capacity for hard disk drives used in data centers and invest $380 million to expand facilities in the Philippines. Toshiba, along with Seagate Technology and Western Digital, are key competitors in the hard disk drive market. Shares of Western Digital dropped 9.8%.

Moderna fell 0.3%. Stock exchange Nasdaq said the biotech and pharma company would replace Warner Bros. Discovery in the Nasdaq 100 before the market opens on Oct. 9. Warner Bros. is set to complete its merger with Paramount Skydance next week.

Twilio declined 1.5%. The cloud communications company technology will join the S&P 500 effective Oct. 6, replacing Warner Bros. Discovery.

Vylor dropped 1.7%. The agricultural technology company joined the S&P 500 Thursday to replace Corteva, which spun off Vylor to separate its seed and advanced genetics business.

data.title: ICE Canada Midday: Canola Rising
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were stronger at midday Friday, continuing their back-and-forth choppy trade of the past week.

November canola was up C$8.60 at C$820.40 per tonne at midsession, with chart-based positioning a feature as values held relatively rangebound.

Gains in Chicago soyoil accounted for some spillover buying interest in the Canadian oilseed, although soybeans were lower.

Seasonal harvest pressure tempered the advances, with warm and dry weather forecast across most of the Prairies over the next week.

Canadian farmers delivered 707,500 tonnes of canola into the commercial pipeline during the week ended Sept. 27, reported the Canadian Grain Commission. That was up 33% from the previous week.

Weekly canola exports of 130,700 tonnes were roughly triple what moved the previous week, bringing the crop-year-to-date total through eight weeks to 921,700 tonnes. That compares with 715,600 tonnes at the same point the previous year.

data.title: G-7 Agrees to Release 100 Million Barrels of Diesel and Crude — WSJ
data.description:
By Matthew Dalton and Kim Mackrael

PARIS-The Group of Seven major economies agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude oil and fuel from their emergency stocks together with allied nations and not to restrict oil exports, the group said, in an effort to bring down the soaring price of diesel and other fuels.

On his Truth Social platform, President Trump said that European nations agreed "to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil. The process will begin immediately."

The release will happen over four months and is aimed at bringing down oil product prices, particularly diesel, the G-7 said.

A statement from French President Emmanuel Macron said the reserve release would aim to bring down oil product prices, particularly diesel.

The announcement would seem to end the threat of a U.S. ban on diesel exports, at least for now. The G-7 countries agreed to "take no measures to restrict the exchange of energy and petroleum products between partner countries," Macron said.

The first batch of the release will give priority to diesel. It will begin immediately and last for 20 days, the group said.

The Iran and Ukraine wars have squeezed exports from two of the world's biggest diesel-producing regions, sending prices to record highs around the globe. The Trump administration had earlier considered restrictions or an outright ban on U.S. exports in an effort to curb prices ahead of next month's midterm elections.

Trump expressed support for a ban last week. Later, though, after a lobbying blitz in Washington by oil companies and their trade groups, he said such a move could cause gasoline prices to rise.

A ban could have been catastrophic for supplies overseas. The rest of the world has relied heavily on U.S. diesel, with much of Middle Eastern and Russian exports blocked from the market.

Executives from ExxonMobil, Chevron, Shell, Phillips 66 and their lobbyists consulted Trump's team on diesel supplies in recent days, advising the administration to pursue alternatives to an outright export ban, some of those people said.

Trump officials have pressed European governments to release more of their emergency fuel stocks onto the market.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote on X Thursday that Europe should deliver on its existing commitments "and make additional supplies immediately available." He said American farmers and businesses shouldn't be "left carrying the burden of a global diesel shortage."

Member nations of the International Energy Agency, a club of Western states and their allies, agreed to release 400 million barrels onto the market in March, the biggest coordinated reserve release in the IEA's history.

European nations have yet to put much of their reserves onto the market. Germany, which has Europe's largest emergency stocks, had released only around 5 million barrels by the end of August, out of an expected 19.5 million that it pledged as part of the IEA announcement.

The G-7 said it would meet with other IEA nations in the coming days to discuss a release of additional diesel reserves to the market.

Write to Matthew Dalton at Matthew.Dalton@wsj.com and Kim Mackrael at kim.mackrael@wsj.com

data.title: Slovak government plans wider deficit in 2027 election year budget
data.description:
Slovakia government will approve its 2027 budget draft on Monday, including plans to widen the deficit heading into elections after years of fiscal consolidation, officials said.

  • The details were agreed at a meeting of the three-party leftist-nationalist ruling coalition on Friday - an accord that sought to ease tensions after a dispute that had threatened its majority.

  • The budget will set out the government's spending plans as it prepares for elections due by September next year.

  • Finance Minister Ladislav Kamenicky said the 2027 budget would target a deficit of 4.94% of gross domestic product.

  • That is up from 4.1% of GDP planned in 2026 - although the state budget watchdog forecasts this year's gap at 4.3% after 4.5% recorded in 2025.

  • Over the last few years, Prime Minister Robert Fico's government had focused on pushing through consolidation packages to try to cut the deficit closer to the European Union's allowed limit of 3% of GDP.

  • "We want Slovakia to have some breathing room after three rounds of fiscal consolidation," Kamenicky said in comments to reporters. Tax hikes were not in the plan, he added.

  • The budget will provide money to help ease energy price hikes, boost salaries and fund drought and transport projects, he said, without going into further details.

  • Parties agreed to cancel a tax on financial transactions from 2028, officials said.

  • The finance ministry this week raised its growth forecast for 2027 to 1.8%, from a previous outlook of 1.5%.

  • Government tensions rose after one of the junior parties in the cabinet voted with the opposition in parliament this week to dismiss the environment minister.

data.title: CoreWeave in focus as UBS sees AI infrastructure market staying hot
data.description:
CoreWeave was in focus on Friday as UBS said it sees the artificial intelligence infrastructure market staying hot.

“There is widespread acknowledgement that the per-hour price of hosted Nvidia GPUs is rising, we are in an inflationary environment, and that revs/GW figures are moving higher, now a key pillar of the hyperscaler and neo-cloud bull case (even though it will take time to work through the P&Ls),” UBS analyst Karl Keirstead wrote in a note to clients. “CoreWeave disclosed this week that it raised per-hour GPU pricing across all SKUs by 25% in July 2026 and that since then (so just in the last 2-3 months) it has raised them by another 10%. 2. Could the new bottleneck of local community and, hence, state/local government pushback throttle the pace of AI data center adds? The risk is real, but the consensus from our checks was that the AI industry will manage through this hurdle as it has with others, and our checks were even more sanguine about this risk than we expected.”

Delving deeper, Keirstead said the availability and the cost of capital could hurt the pace of the AI buildout. Recent checks have concluded some projects will wind up fading, but the “better-positioned players” will not have an issue, Keirstead added, including CoreWeave.

data.title: Wages Are Rising at the Slowest Pace Since 2021 — WSJ
data.description:
By Konrad Putzier

A month before the midterms, the cost-of-living squeeze is showing signs of worsening.

Average hourly earnings growth slowed to 3.0% in September, down from 3.1% in August, according to new Labor Department data. That's the lowest growth since May 2021, when the economy was still recovering from the pandemic shock.

Meanwhile, inflation remains stubbornly high, and the cost of gasoline, diesel and airfares has surged since the start of the Iran war. Consumer prices rose 3.4% in August, the latest data available. That means many Americans are getting pinched from two sides.

Wages "are having a hard time keeping up with inflation," said Tom Porcelli, chief economist at Wells Fargo.

That weakness in real incomes helps explain why many Americans are feeling glum about the economy despite low unemployment and healthy GDP growth. Consumer confidence is near historic lows, according to a recent University of Michigan survey.

And this comes after years of runaway price growth already eating into wages: A significant minority of households saw their real incomes fall in the five years ending in 2025.

data.title: MK Stalin calls Vijay "reels" CM, urges voters to back DMK in Dharapuram bypoll
data.description:
Dharapuram, Oct. 2 -- Ahead of the Dharapuram by-election on October 6, DMK president and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin on Friday lauched a sharp attack on the ruling TVK government while addressing a campaign meeting in support of the DMK candidate S Suganya.

Stalin labelled the Chief Minister Vijay as the "Reels" CM, urging people to vote for DMK to give a "fitting reply" to the CM.

"To give a fitting reply to the arrogance of the 'Reels' Chief Minister who lacks the support of the majority of the people, to safeguard the honour of Dharapuram, vote for the Rising Sun symbol on October 6th and ensure the victory of our sister advocate Suganya," he said on X, sharing a glimpse of his rally in Dharapuram.

In his address to the people during the campaign, Stalin referred to the beauty of the Amaravathi River and the town's historical significance. He described Dharapuram as a place known for supplying quality paddy seeds to other regions and said the people of the constituency were actively involved in agriculture.

"I have not come here merely to seek votes. I have come seeking justice", said Stalin.

Referring to Vijay's last film, Stalin said, "He acted in a film titled Jananayagan, but today he is acting like a villain to democracy." He also alleged that TVK had acknowledged its political proximity to the BJP and said he welcomed the acceptance.

"He admitted that they are a branch of the BJP. He admitted that TVK is just a branch of the BJP. I am glad that he spoke that truth," said Stalin.

Stalin criticised Vijay over his political style and alleged that his gestures had lowered the dignity of the Legislative Assembly, saying, "Behave like a Chief Minister, not a 'cheap minister '" also accusing the TVK of functioning more like a corporate organisation than a political party.

He alleged that government employees across various departments were staging protests and claimed that people in several areas were facing prolonged power cuts.

He also criticised the state government over alleged electricity tariffs, rising prices, and the Cauvery water dispute with Karnataka. "Instead of merely reading newspapers, take action and do something beneficial for farmers", he said.

On law and order, Stalin alleged that the government had failed to control drug sales and referred to figures relating to murders. He questioned the status of the government's "Singappen" initiative and alleged that ministers were being asked to respond whenever questions were raised about law and order.

"If you open the news, five murders, eight murders in a single day-people are being hacked to death in heaps! If someone tips off the police about narcotics, the informant gets murdered! No action is taken against those peddling drugs," he said.

Stalin also alleged that "investment intended for Tamil Nadu had gone to neighbouring Andhra Pradesh."

Listing the DMK government's previous welfare initiatives, Stalin said his government had introduced schemes intended to benefit every family.

He said that Tamil Nadu was the first state in India to introduce free bus travel for women, said that Rs 87 crore had been allocated for industrial development in Dharapuram, and alleged that certain works were being undertaken even before tenders had been issued. He also referred to expenditure on releasing water from the Mettur reservoir.

Stalin claimed that if the ruling party win the by-election, electricity charges and milk prices could increase, adding that "this by-election is not merely about Dharapuram. You have the responsibility of protecting the interests of the entire Tamil Nadu."

The bypolls will be held in Dharapuram and Madurantakam assembly constituencies on October 6, with counting of votes scheduled on October 9.

data.title: European aluminium premium hits highest since June on supply concerns
data.description:
Aluminium premiums in Europe have jumped to their highest level in almost four months, with two industry sources attributing the jump to concerns that a potential cut in US tariffs on Canadian metal could leave the continent short of supply.

The front-month COMEX European duty-paid aluminium premium (EPDc1), paid on top of benchmark London Metal Exchange aluminium prices for physical metal, rose to $574 a metric ton on Thursday, up 10% from the previous day and the highest since June 8, LSEG data showed on Friday.

  • The European premium has been rising in recent weeks on reports that US President Donald Trump's 50% tariff on aluminium imports could be halved to 25% for material from neighbouring Canada.

  • Talks between Washington and Ottawa collapsed in mid-August, but Trump said on Monday he thinks a trade deal with Canada will be made.

  • A tariff cut would allow more Canadian metal to flow to the US; EU imports of aluminium from Canada rose by 80% year on year in January-July to 269,839 tons as the bloc sought to make up for shortfalls from the war-hit Middle East.

  • While supply in Europe remains tight, the COMEX Japan aluminium premium (PJMc1), a reference price for the Asian market, has fallen by 35% since the end of July and this week hit $226 a ton, its lowest since mid-March.

  • "Asian aluminium premiums are retreating as inventories build and underlying demand remains weak," consultancy CRU said in a recent note, adding that new capacity in 2027 would reach Asia first and could apply further pressure.

  • Three-month aluminium on the LME fell for a fifth day on Friday, touching $3,105 a ton, its lowest since July 7.

data.title: Nymex Overview: Petroleum Futures Falling on News of Planned G7 Inventory Release — OPIS
data.description:
Crude oil and refined product futures contracts were seeing sharp declines Friday amid increased optimism over Middle East oil supply and news that the Group of Seven nations plan a substantial release from diesel and crude stockpiles to combat record-high prices.

U.S. oil prices were down about 2.4% at 11:45 a.m. ET, with the November West Texas Intermediate crude prices down $2.12 to $90.75/bbl and December prices trading $1.98 lower to $88.91/bbl.

Brent crude losses were lighter, with the December contract moving 96cts lower to $101.35/bbl and January prices sinking by 68cts to $97.75/bbl.

Diesel futures were falling by about 3.8%, with November prices off by 17.5cts to $4.467/gal and the December contract 16.45cts lower to $4.3261/gal.

RBOB futures were trading down 3.4%, with the November contract sinking by 11.54cts to $3.2872/gal and December prices moving 8.4cts lower to $3.0889/gal.

If the declines hold, they will snap a two-day streak of solid gains for both crude and ULSD.

Prices are weakening after the G7 nations said they planned to release 100 million barrels from their stored reserves of diesel and crude over the next four months.

A statement from the group encouraged countries with significant refining capacity to boost production. It said member countries will also "coordinate maintenance schedules across G7 refineries to prevent simultaneous capacity shutdowns and temporarily increase utilization rates where feasible."

The move comes as U.S. President Donald Trump has been criticizing European leaders, saying they have not significantly tapped into their reserves to help address rising fuel costs amid the Iran war.

Prices are also being pressured by recent news of larger-than-expected oil shipments from the Middle East, even as uncertainty remains about the future of the ongoing Iranian conflict.

Petroleum prices had moved higher earlier in the week following reports the U.S. was sending a third aircraft carrier to the region, raising the possibility of an impending increase in fighting.
